findings.fix: (1) axe color-contrast, 11 nodes: --red on its own 18% tint measures 4.35:1, under the 4.5 AA floor for text that small. The gold pair already clears at 5.41:1, so only the red needed lifting -- #fca5a5 on the same tint is 6.35:1. Lifted the text rather than darkening the tint, because the tint is what makes a red pill READ as red. (2) Six hail/quote fields plus two feedback filters sat at 13.3px/12.8px; below 16px iOS Safari zooms on focus and never zooms back, so a buyer tapping 'address' mid-hail is thrown into a magnified horizontally-scrolling page. Fixed on the SHARED _svcInputC constant so a seventh field inherits the fix instead of re-introducing the bug. (3) CLS 0.468 ('poor', budget 0.1) on platform-actions: four queues each painted a one-line 'Loading...' then grew, shoving every card below them down -- the founder could press Reject on a row that had just become a different row. Now the queues fill while #actions is still hidden and the layout lands once, with a finally{} so a failed fetch still reveals the page.

This is not about the credits.' sybil: second claim returns {"reason": "already_claimed", "granted": false}. collusive pair: a naked user-to-user transfer REFUSED with 'Credits cannot be moved between people. They are earned on a purchase and spent on a purchase' and circulation delta exactly 0.00. scam provider: the buyer gets a dated deadline (2026-08-06) and raise_service_objection returns {ok:true}, moving the job to disputed.
findings.why_it_matters: The 500-run simulation proved the ECONOMICS hold. It never proved the SCREEN refuses these people in words they can act on -- and a guard that blocks in silence cannot be told apart from a guard that is not firing at all. So each persona asserts two things, and a bare 'violates check constraint' fails the readability bar.
findings.note: THE PROBE'S OWN THREE BUGS ARE WHY IT IS TRUSTWORTHY, and each is a banked class. (1) It read only stdout while every verdict line is a psql NOTICE on stderr -- all four reported 'no verdict line', a false red. (2) It probed the spam cap with NO JWT, and guard_first_listings_need_a_sale opens with `if auth.uid() is null return new` (the backend path seeders need), so all 8 listings published and it read as 'the cap does not work' when the probe was never a person -- the 'an RLS probe needs the ROLE, not just claims' lesson, applied to a trigger. (3) Even with an identity, TWO earlier guards fired first: self-publish is refused outright, then the reservation guard refused for want of credits -- so the cap was never consulted and a PASS proved only the outermost gate, the 'survivor masked by a sibling constraint' shape. It now funds the seller and selects one already AT the cap by the cap's own arithmetic, so the deepest layer is the one that answers. Registered in run_platform_checks as gate `adversarial-personas`.

evidence.asserts: the spammer is capped with a reason they can act on, the sybil is refused a second starter grant, a collusive pair extracts EXACTLY 0, and a scam provider's job cannot pass the window unnoticed
evidence.checked:
THE TOP-UP RAIL, END TO END, AGAINST THE LEDGER. Three top-ups exist and each is exactly where it should be: ₱1,000 verified -> exactly ONE ledger row of ₱1,000; ₱500 verified -> exactly ONE row of ₱500; ₱300 pending_verification -> ZERO rows. Credits are not minted until a human verifies the GCash reference, so the ledger totals 1,500 while 1,800 has been filed -- that gap is the verification gate working, not a discrepancy, and it is worth writing down because it looks like one at a glance.
Balances derive from those rows and nothing else: David Velasco Electrical 1,000 (his top-up); Christine Dizon HVAC 340 (500 - 80 - 80 commission); Pablo Aguilar Calibration -200 (a legacy commission with no top-up behind it). Checked through provider_credit_balance() and seller_credit_balance(), which agree at the person level even though Pablo holds TWO provider rows, one per hive -- no double count.
A NEGATIVE BALANCE IS THE INTERESTING CASE and this surface handles it properly: '₱-200 · Available to list · Below zero, so publishing is paused: a listing needs 10% of its price held in credits. Top up by ₱200 to clear this, plus the hold for whatever you list next.' with a 'Go to top up' route. The number, the consequence, the reason, the exact amount to clear it, and the way out. Measured on a plain RELOAD, not after a hand-called refresh, which is the half of this oracle that usually rots.
